meta.name: Send nightly staging vs production drift digest from Google Sheets with Snapshot Site and Slack

name: Nightly Staging vs Production Drift Digest → Slack

parameters.content:
## Nightly Staging vs Production Drift Digest → Slack

### How it works

Every night this workflow reads a list of paths from a Google Sheet (`path`, `label`), joins each one onto a **production base URL** and a **staging base URL**, and runs a single Snapshot Site **Compare** call per path with the production URL as `beforeUrl` and the staging URL as `afterUrl`. Compare captures both sides itself, so one path costs **one** API call — not two Screenshots plus a Compare. No baseline images are stored anywhere: both sides are live. Each result is bucketed into a drift band (identical / minor / significant / severe) and, when the loop finishes, rendered as one Slack digest sorted worst-first. A path that cannot be reached is recorded as `failed` and the loop continues, so one dead path never costs you the whole report.

### Setup steps

- Install the `n8n-nodes-snapshot-site` community node (Settings → Community nodes → Install → `n8n-nodes-snapshot-site`) — verified by n8n.
- Add a Snapshot Site credential, a Google Sheets credential, and a Slack credential.
- Create a **Paths** tab and type this header row literally into row 1, one column per cell: `path`, `label`. Cell **A1 must contain the literal text `path`**, not a path or a URL — otherwise Google Sheets' `read` operation treats that value as the column name, `$json.path` is `undefined` for every row, and every Compare call fails.
- Fill one row per page: `path` = the route only (`/`, `/pricing`, `/blog/hello`), `label` = a short human name for the digest.
- Open **Build Environment URL Pair** and edit the two constants at the top — `PROD_BASE` and `STAGING_BASE`. Both must include `https://`; the API rejects a bare domain with a soft error. They live in one node deliberately: two hardcoded bases in two different nodes drift apart.
- ⚠️ **Keep `beforeOptions` and `afterOptions` byte-identical** on **Compare Staging to Production**. A different `width`, or `hideCookie` on one side only, manufactures permanent false drift on every single path — and that noise is indistinguishable from real drift. If you edit one option, edit the other in the same breath.
- Point **Read Staging Path List** at your spreadsheet, set the channel on both Slack nodes, and adjust the schedule.

### Customization

Tune the drift bands in **Record Drift Result** (`MINOR_DRIFT_PCT`, `SIGNIFICANT_DRIFT_PCT`, `SEVERE_DRIFT_PCT`) rather than adding a flat changed/unchanged gate — a nightly staging diff is never zero, because staging is legitimately ahead of production. Grow the `hide` selector list (on BOTH sides) to mask anything time-based instead of raising thresholds. Swap the all-clear message for a No Operation node if you want true silence, and raise `settings.executionTimeout` for a long path list, since the Compare calls run sequentially.

## Schedule and build the URL pair

Runs once a night and reads every watched path from the Google Sheet (`path`, `label`).
One Code node joins each path onto `PROD_BASE` and `STAGING_BASE` — the only two values you edit — and normalises slashes so no side ever gets a `//` URL.

## Compare both environments and handle errors

ONE Compare call per path: production as `beforeUrl`, staging as `afterUrl`, both captured live by the API. Two Screenshots plus a Compare would triple the cost for the same answer.
`beforeOptions` and `afterOptions` are byte-identical — any asymmetry (different width, `hideCookie` on one side) manufactures permanent false drift on every path.
Hard failures (error output) and soft failures (`{error: true}` on the success output) are both recorded as `failed` and returned to the loop, never aborting the digest.

## Report the nightly drift bands

On the loop's Done branch, results are sorted by mismatch descending and counted per band — identical / minor / significant / severe — because a nightly staging diff is never zero and a boolean gate would fire every night.
Only severe, significant, or failed paths trigger the full digest; a quiet night still posts a short all-clear so silence always means "workflow broken".
